Theme

School & learning · Time, the calendar & feasts

school year noun

also academic year, school years, new school year

modern

Levi–Bini p. 271: per tōtum annum scholasticum

annus scholasticus

the school year

Scholasticus, of the schools, is post-Augustan (Quint., Plin. Ep., Lewis & Short); the phrase is modern. At the start of the school year, ineunte annō scholasticō (see at the beginning of the year).

Examples

  • Ineunte annō scholasticō novōs librōs ēmimus.

    At the start of the school year we bought new books.composed

See also term, year, holidays, school, break, at the beginning of the year.

SourcesLewis & Short: annus · Lewis & Short: scholasticus

Enrico Levi and Arturo Bini, Il latino come lingua viva (1937), p. 271.

The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.
